column3: Pairs the same promise formula with truthfulness, framing 77:7 as an assured occurrence while retaining promise as benefit or threat.
Gives the Day of Distinction a fixed collective appointment, specifying the scheduled setting in which 77:7 occurs.
Shows a word becoming operative upon its people; a secondary parallel to the announced matter becoming binding event.
Uses the same occurrence predicate for recompense, including both settled consequence and a secondary debt-settlement reading.
Begins the oath sequence leading to 77:7 and preserves its commissioned-movement framing without resolving its referent.
Presents a previously promised punishment as now demonstratively present, giving 77:7 a later fulfilled horizon.
Identifies a promised outcome with the Day of Account, locating one possible content of 77:7.
The immediately preceding excuse-or-warning clause supplies the communicative function of the oath sequence before 77:7.
Directly calls the Lord's punishment an occurring reality; its cosmic context also keeps a secondary impact reading in view.
Preserves a contrary response that treats what is promised as implausibly remote.
Asks for which day matters were deferred, extending 77:7 from certainty to an appointed time.
Names the occurrence itself and, with its ensuing upheaval, supports both settled-event and forceful-impact readings.
Joins provision with what is promised, keeping the promise's recipient-dependent benefit/threat range open.
Connects cosmic observation with the possible nearness of an appointed end; useful for timing, not for fixing content.
Names the promised day as a definite rendezvous bearing both assurance and threat for different recipients.
Names the event as having occurred amid sweeping cosmic collapse, concretizing a forceful realization reading.
Continues the oath sequence with violent motion, preserving the lead-in imagery without identifying it.
Links accumulated messenger-rejection to a warning becoming due and effective, adding a responsibility trajectory.
States that the promised matter comes by divine will and cannot be escaped, reinforcing inevitability without a date.
Places the messengers at an appointed time, developing the scheduling strand immediately before 77:7's later exposition.
Preserves the demand for the promise's date as a skeptical test of truth, rather than a disproof of 77:7.
Portrays a counted, measured delay, supporting appointed timing rather than immediate fulfillment.
States the woe for deniers in the unfolding Day of Distinction material, giving 77:7 a judicial consequence.
Makes prior warning procedurally relevant at judgment, including the distinction between shared expectation and opposite outcomes.
Withholds knowledge of timing while presenting clear warning, preserving certainty without date disclosure.
Describes the Hour as fixed, weighty, and sudden; strongly clarifies timing while leaving the exact hour unknown.
Uses competing future promise and threat as a secondary analogy for recipient-conditioned expectation, not 77:7's event.
The occurrence concerns enmity produced by a practice, not the promised eschatological realization.
Continues the oath sequence through spreading or distribution imagery; it supplies context but no settled referent.
Denies that the event's occurrence can be falsified, directly sharpening 77:7's certainty.
Presents a promised outcome as addressed to guarded returners, preserving a beneficial recipient-specific horizon.
Names the deferred day as the Day of Distinction, directly identifying the setting developed after 77:7.
Calls punishment an occurring reality and preserves both a demanded-punishment reading and a secondary distant-versus-certain contrast.
States that what is promised is coming and inescapable, closely reinforcing 77:7's inevitability.
Part of the cosmic sequence surrounding the appointed Day, giving visible transformation to 77:7's realization.
Explains repeated warning as producing caution or renewed remembrance, clarifying the warning side of what is promised.
Keeps the promised matter certain while explicitly leaving its nearness or extended term unresolved.
Shows affliction prompting a conditional pledge; a secondary contrast between relief-seeking promise and durable fulfillment.
Preserves a contrary challenge to post-death emergence; secondarily, it frames death as not necessarily final.
The statement of deprivation adds no clear promise, occurrence, or appointment relation to 77:7.
Continues the oath sequence with separating action, anticipating the later Day of Distinction without deciding the oath referent.
Calls Hell the appointed meeting-place for all of them, specifying one threat-side destination of 77:7.
A claim of anger supplies no material clarification of 77:7.
Intensifies the Day of Distinction question, preserving its weight and undisclosed full character.
Contrasts pre-event impatience with post-occurrence belief, showing that realization can close the time for responsive trust.
The repeated deprivation statement adds no clear promise, occurrence, or appointment relation to 77:7.
The living-and-dead pairing later in the surah offers only a broad mortality context for the promised event.
Shows the word becoming effective because of wrongdoing and silencing rebuttal, a strong realization-and-liability parallel.
Keeps the promised matter's near-or-far timing unknown while maintaining its announced horizon.
A fixed term for lifted affliction and subsequent breach adds a limited appointment-and-delay parallel.
The trumpet turns warning into a public event called the Day of Warning, giving a concrete trigger for 77:7.
Addresses recipients with their promised day, moving the promise from distant expectation to present allocation.
The casting of remembrance immediately precedes 77:7, preserving the delivered-warning strand of the oath sequence.
States that what had been promised eventually came after extended enjoyment, distinguishing delay from cancellation.
Preserves a promise of the Garden for the steadfast, showing that what is promised need not be threat alone.
Cosmic opening is part of the surrounding sequence and supports the visible upheaval associated with 77:7.
Declares the divine promise true and warns against worldly deception, strongly supporting the promise's reliability.
Shows truth becoming established while crafted falsehood fails; a secondary realization contrast rather than an appointment account.
The heart-and-hearing response offers only a secondary reception-of-reminder link to the warning preceding 77:7.
Preserves a contrary demand that threatened proof arrive at once, exposing a contest over timing.
Human threatening along a path is a lexical contrast, not evidence about the promised event of 77:7.
The effacement of stars is the first explicit cosmic sign after 77:7, supporting a visible upheaval horizon.
Preserves the contrary dismissal of a long-repeated promise as old tales, while timing remains beyond its recipients' control.
The ordered positions of stars supply a secondary cosmic-order parallel, not an identification of 77:7's event.
Later refusal of permission to apologize gives a consequence-side detail of the realized judgment.
Preserves a defiant demand that the promised consequence be brought, a contrary posture toward 77:7's certainty.
Deferred respite leading to increased wrongdoing supplies only a broad delay-before-punishment pattern.
Records doubt about the true promise and the Hour, preserving a contrary response to certainty.
Distinguishes whether the promised result is shown to the messenger from the certainty of power to realize it.
Links an un-doubted day, gathering, and non-breach of appointment, strengthening the fixed-appointment frame.
A later image of sparks supplies a punishment scene but adds little to the occurrence claim itself.
Names the Hour as their appointment and a graver future event, giving 77:7 a decisive appointment horizon.
A false self-description as reformers does not clarify the promise or occurrence in 77:7.
The command concerning deniers has only a remote contrast with 77:7's denier-directed warning.
The final promise gathers people after an interim dwelling, adding a delayed-assembly reading.
This command about evil speech has no material relation to 77:7's promised event.
Pairs some shown promised outcomes with death, proclamation, and accounting; timing remains under divine control.
The promised fire reverses hostile posture into an impending consequence, adding a threat-side reversal.
Fear from Satan does not materially explain 77:7's promise or realization.
A challenge to produce comparable discourse has only a remote contrast through truth-claim and denial.
A mutually fixed time and place illustrate appointment, but in a bounded human contest rather than 77:7's event.
Immediate fire imagery for injustice offers a general punishment parallel, not the announced occurrence.
A ruler's claim about conquest supplies no reliable link to 77:7 beyond auxiliary lexical resonance.
Woe for deniers on their promised day closely joins promised timing, threat, and recipient response.
A past battle lapse and pardon do not materially clarify 77:7.
The exchange about a gift has no material relation to 77:7.
Fear of standing and warning supplies a general ethical consequence, not the promised event's realization.
Hypocritical mockery adds no material clarification of 77:7.
A reward becoming due upon death is a distant occurrence analogy, not evidence about the promised Day.
Rules of repentance do not materially clarify 77:7.
An excuse about ancestral association does not add to the promise or occurrence in 77:7.
A completed forty-night appointment is a limited timing analogy without an eschatological realization link.
Calls the divine promise true and makes it regulate present caution, reinforcing certainty with ethical force.
Manipulating calendar months is not evidence about the promised occurrence in 77:7.
Keeps the divine promise unbroken amid recurring calamities, treating interim events as warning rather than failed fulfillment.
Return to the Creator supplies a broad destination frame but no specific promise or occurrence clarification.
States that the divine promise is true and the Hour lacks doubt, offering a direct certainty parallel.
Creation and prohibition of associates do not materially clarify 77:7.
A social-status challenge on recitation does not add to the promised event of 77:7.
The account of later followers and reward does not materially clarify 77:7.
Prayer for what was promised through the messengers connects promise with the final non-disgrace horizon.
Calls the believers' promised outcome true, preserving a benefit-side counterpart to threat readings.
A promise of forgiveness and great reward confirms that the promise formula can carry a positive destination.
Both parties report finding their Lord's promise true, giving fulfilled promise a reciprocal judgment-scene form.
A historical divine promise of one party illustrates fulfillment but does not clarify 77:7's final event.
A binding promise of Paradise across revelations supplies a covenantal benefit-side parallel.
Calls the divine promise true and links return with renewed creation, directly supplying an eschatological horizon.
Preserves the recurring contrary demand for the date of the promise.
Answers whether the announced matter is true with an emphatic affirmation and inescapability.
Declares the divine promise true while noting that many do not know, closely pairing certainty with denial.
Delays punishment to a numbered term, supporting measured postponement rather than cancellation.
Describes the hereafter as a day for gathering and witnessing, clarifying the collective realization horizon.
Says that day is deferred only to a numbered term, sharpening appointed timing.
Denies that the divine promise to messengers can fail, giving a direct reliability statement.
Contrasts a true divine promise with a false satanic promise, clarifying promise reliability by opposition.
Announces that the divine command has come and forbids haste, a direct event-arrival parallel.
Calls resurrection a binding divine promise, explicitly joining promise, truth, and return from death.
The latter promise arrives with a consequential visitation, supplying an earlier-or-later fulfillment pattern.
Calls the Lord's promise true when it comes and levels what stood, joining realization to visible transformation.
Describes the promised Garden as an assured promise, preserving a positive destination reading.
States that the Hour is coming, retaining certainty while its disclosure remains withheld.
Reports fulfillment of the promise to messengers and the survival of those willed, a historical fulfillment parallel.
Names a coming cosmic transformation as a binding promise that will be carried out.
States that the Hour is coming without doubt and that those in graves will be raised.
Says the divine promise is never broken while addressing demands to hasten punishment.
Asks for protection should the threatened matter be shown, treating it as a realizable impending outcome.
Affirms power to show the messenger what the opponents are promised, separating certainty from visibility.
Calls the requested abiding good a binding promise, retaining a benefit-side destination.
Preserves another contrary question about when the promise will come.
Makes recognition of the divine promise's truth the result of a return and reunion.
Contrasts one who meets a good promise with one given temporary worldly enjoyment.
States that whoever hopes for meeting God finds His term coming, linking expectation to appointed arrival.
Names the divine promise true while retaining the contrast of widespread lack of knowledge.
Names the Day of Decision and portrays belief then as no longer beneficial, clarifying the realized verdict.
Presents the divine and messenger promise as confirmed in a moment of trial, preserving a faithful reception reading.
Asks for the promise's date in the context of a day of gathering and separation.
Answers with a fixed day whose time cannot be delayed or advanced.
Preserves the deniers' question about when the promise will occur.
Identifies resurrection as what the Merciful promised and the messengers confirmed.
States that the divine promise is not broken while describing a promised reward horizon.
Calls the divine promise true in a setting of forgiveness and future vindication.
States that the Hour is coming without doubt, closely reinforcing 77:7's certainty.
Distinguishes showing some of the promise from taking the messenger while affirming the return to divine judgment.
Reserves knowledge of the Hour with God, preserving certainty without accessible timing.
Links the revealed measure with the possible nearness of the Hour.
Describes the Hour as arriving suddenly while people are unaware.
Preserves a contrary denial of the promise of post-death raising.
Tells the messenger not to hasten: when they see what was promised, its delay will appear brief.
Describes the Hour as possibly coming suddenly, supporting the sudden-arrival strand.
Reports fulfillment of a true vision; it is a secondary model of promise verified in history.
The removal of the veil supplies a later disclosure scene for a realized event.
Swears that the announced matter is true, immediately reinforcing the preceding promise language.
Commands that deniers be left until the day they are struck, adding a deferred-consequence horizon.
States that the Hour has drawn near, directly strengthening imminence without fixing its date.
Counters denial of resurrection with an oath that all will be raised and informed.
Preserves the question of when the promise comes, alongside the surrounding warning context.
Preserves the view that the promised event is far away, a contrary timing assessment.
Sets against it the view that the same event is near, retaining the unresolved contrast.
Counters the assumption that bones will not be gathered, supplying a resurrection-side implication.
Asks when the Day of Resurrection will be, preserving the timing question.
Names the Day of Decision as an appointed time, directly paralleling 77:12-13.
Asks about the Hour's anchoring time, preserving a timing inquiry without granting its answer.
